content:
The image shows a mango leaf with dark, irregular black spots and patches scattered across the surface. The leaf is green but heavily covered with small to medium black sooty deposits, concentrated in clusters. There is no white powdery coating (ruling out Powdery Mildew), no stem dieback, and no typical anthracnose lesions with yellow halos. The black, superficial, smudgy deposits covering the leaf surface are characteristic of sooty mold — a fungal growth on honeydew secreted by sap-sucking insects.
